claims.claim: NuScale addresses a real firm-power bottleneck for load growth through modular nuclear generation, but the causal chain still requires project financing, licensing/site execution, module fabrication and customer deployment before technical readiness becomes delivered infrastructure.
Supplier engineering and component production reduce technical implementation uncertainty but do not establish customer-funded deployment economics.

factors.name: alignment2036
factors.basis: firm low-carbon generation can serve rising electricity demand where grid capacity and reliability are constraints

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: approved design/IP matters, but financing, construction, licensing and supply chain remain successor bottlenecks

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: SMRs can fit constrained grids and industrial loads, but compete with conventional nuclear, gas plus carbon constraints, renewables/storage and grid expansion

risks.risk: Successor bottlenecks are financing, customer commitment, licensing/site construction and cost competitiveness rather than module design alone.

causalEdges.mechanism: customers with reliability/decarbonization needs may value modular nuclear capacity
causalEdges.falsifier: customers consistently choose cheaper/faster substitutes and binding NuScale deployments fail to materialize

causalEdges.mechanism: engineering maturity enables fabrication but must pass financing, licensing and construction gates
causalEdges.falsifier: projects remain unfunded/unbuilt despite component progress

unknowns.unknown: Binding project-level customer economics and realized construction cost remain unproven.

claims.claim: Dilution is a present, material risk rather than a hypothetical falsifier: NuScale sold 89,727,165 Class A shares during the first six months of 2026 for about $1.0B gross/$984.5M net proceeds.
The balance sheet is substantially funded, but commercialization remains loss-making: the company reported an $824.4M accumulated deficit and negative operating cash flows since inception.

factors.name: financing/dilution
factors.basis: 2026 ATM issuance materially expanded equity while funding commercialization

factors.name: execution risk
factors.basis: technical milestones coexist with continuing operating losses and unproven deployment economics

risks.risk: Future capital needs can transfer commercialization risk to shareholders through dilution even if technical milestones continue.
Substitute generation/storage solutions may reach customers faster or at lower delivered cost.

causalEdges.mechanism: continued development and commercialization spending requires capital before recurring project cash generation
causalEdges.falsifier: binding deployments generate sufficient cash and project funding to materially reduce corporate equity dependence

contradictions.claim: Physical component production indicates progress, but it does not resolve the financial contradiction of heavy equity issuance and negative operating cash flow.
contradictions.resolution: Treat technical progress as positive execution evidence while retaining dilution/commercialization risk as non-gating present risk.

unknowns.unknown: Ultimate overnight cost, customer financing structure and recurring economics of first commercial plants remain unknown.
